'''Egon Balas''' (June 7, 1922 in [[Cluj, Romania|Cluj]], Romania – March 18, 2019)<ref>{{cite web |title=Remembering Egon Balas |url=https://www.cmu.edu/tepper/news/stories/2019/march/egon-balas.html?hootPostID=6cde4cd465b0167e1b3c4ef18ca960f1 |access-date=20 March 2019 |archive-date=27 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190327101400/https://www.cmu.edu/tepper/news/stories/2019/march/egon-balas.html?hootPostID=6cde4cd465b0167e1b3c4ef18ca960f1 |url-status=dead }}</ref> was an [[Applied mathematics|applied mathematician]] and a [[professor]] of industrial administration and applied mathematics at [[Carnegie Mellon University]]. He was the Thomas Lord Professor of Operations Research at Carnegie Mellon's [[Tepper School of Business]] and did fundamental work in developing [[integer programming|integer and disjunctive programming]].<ref>* Graham K. Rand: Egon Balas, ''Profiles in Operations Research'' (eds.: A.A. Asad, S.L. Gass), International Series in Operations Research and Management Science, 147, Springer, 2011.</ref>

== Life and education ==
Balas was born in [[Cluj-Napoca|Cluj]] (Romania) in a [[Hungarian Jewish]] family. His original name was Blatt, which was first changed to the Hungarian Balázs and then later to the Romanian Balaş. He was married to art historian [[Edith Balas]], a survivor of Auschwitz, with whom he had two daughters.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cmu.edu/cas/people/balas_edith.html|title=Edith Balas - Center for the Arts in Society - Carnegie Mellon University|first=Carnegie Mellon|last=University|website=www.cmu.edu|access-date=8 October 2017|archive-date=27 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190327101402/https://www.cmu.edu/cas/people/balas_edith.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cmu.edu/news/archive/2011/March/march22_edithbalasmemoir.shtml|title=March 22: CMU's Edith Balas Pens Memoir Depicting Life as a Survivor and Scholar - Carnegie Mellon University - CMU|first=Carnegie Mellon University|last=(CMU)|website=www.cmu.edu|access-date=8 October 2017|archive-date=8 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171008231423/https://www.cmu.edu/news/archive/2011/March/march22_edithbalasmemoir.shtml|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was imprisoned by the Communist authorities for several years after the war.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://holocaustcenterpgh.org/exhibitions/in-celebration-of-life-living-legacy-project/edith-balas/|title=Holocaust Center of Pittsburgh » Edith Balas|website=holocaustcenterpgh.org|access-date=8 October 2017|archive-date=8 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171008231130/http://holocaustcenterpgh.org/exhibitions/in-celebration-of-life-living-legacy-project/edith-balas/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He left Romania in 1966 and accepted an appointment with [[Carnegie Mellon University]] in 1967. Balas obtained a "Diploma Licentiate" in [[economics]] ([[Babeș-Bolyai University|Bolyai University]], 1949) and [[Ph.D.]]s in economics ([[Free University of Brussels (1834–1969)|University of Brussels]], 1967) and mathematics ([[University of Paris]], 1968).<ref>E. Balas: ''Will to Freedom: A Perilous Journey through Fascism and Communism'' (Syracuse University Press, 2000)</ref> 
His mathematics PhD thesis was titled ''Minimax et dualité en programmation discrète'' and was written under the direction of [[Robert Fortet]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=154872}}</ref>

===Selected publications===
*E. Balas, A. Saxena: Optimizing Over the Split Closure, ''Mathematical Programming'' 113, 2 (2008), 219–240.
*E. Balas, M. Perregaard: A Precise Correspondence Between Lift-and-Project Cuts, Simple Disjunctive Cuts, and Mixed Integer Gomory Cuts for 0-1 Programming, ''Mathematical Programming'' B (94), 2003; 221–245.
*E. Balas, S. Ceria, [[Gérard Cornuéjols|G. Cornuéjols]]: Mixed 0-1 Programming by Lift-and-Project in a Branch-and-Cut Framework,  ''Management Science'' 42, 1996; 1229–1246.
*E. Balas: The Prize Collecting Traveling Salesman Problem: II Polyhedral Results, ''Networks'' 25, 1995; 199–216. 
*E. Balas, S. Ceria, [[Gérard Cornuéjols|G. Cornuéjols]]: A Lift-and-Project Cutting Plane Algorithm for Mixed 0-1 Programs, ''Mathematical Programming'' 58, 1993; 295–324.
*E. Balas: The Prize Collecting Traveling Salesman Problem I, ''Networks'' 19, 1989; 621–636.
*E. Balas, J. Adams, D. Zawack: The Shifting Bottleneck Procedure for Job Shop Scheduling, ''Management Science'' 34, 1988; 391–401. 
*E. Balas, V. Chvátal, J. Nesetril: On The Maximum-Weight Clique Problem,  ''Mathematics of Operations Research'' 12, 1987; 522–536.
*E. Balas: Disjunctive Programming, ''Annals of Discrete Mathematics'' 5, 1979; 3–51.
*E. Balas: An Additive Algorithm for Linear Programming in Zero-One Variables, ''Operations Research'' 13 (4), 1965; 517–546.

===Honors and awards===
* National Academy of Engineering, 2006
* IFORS Hall of Fame, 2006
* Honorary Doctorate in Mathematics, University of Waterloo, 2005
* Hungarian Academy of Science, external member, 2004
* INFORMS Fellow, 2002
* Honorary Doctorate in Mathematics, Miguel Hernandez University, Elche, Spain, 2002
* [[EURO Gold Medal]], 2001
* John von Neumann Theory Prize, INFORMS, 1995
* Senior U.S. Scientist Award of the von Humboldt Foundation, 1980–1981
